inputs.original_text: PARIS, France— In a case that has sent ripples of concern through religious communities and civil liberties advocates across France, a French abbot has been convicted under a controversial new law targeting “psychological subjection.” The conviction of Father Bernard Domini, superior of the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame (FMND), under France’s new law has ignited a [...]
inputs.modified_text: This is about more than one conviction. France’s new “psychological subjection” law gives authorities a convenient, elastic label to use against communities they want to bring into line. Father Bernard Domini, the abbot leading the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame, is being made an example, while the public is being asked to see it as protection. That’s how control becomes normalized: officials decide which beliefs are dangerous, then use vague language to make dissent look like a threat. Today it’s this community; the precedent could be used against anyone inconvenient.
